indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.3.1.1: (Content standard garbled in source document)
indicator.objective: Identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest)

skills.description: Name external body parts correctly when shown or pointed to
Identify/point to a named body part on self or on a picture
Say where a body part is found
Draw and label at least three external body parts

misconceptions: The chest is the same as the stomach.
Fingers and toes are the same.
Shoulders are part of the arm only.

questions.stem: Which part of the body do we use to see?
questions.explanation: We use our eyes to see.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the eyes with other facial parts.

questions.stem: Which part of the body do we use to hear?
hints: It is on the side of your head.
questions.explanation: We use our ears to hear.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think they hear with their eyes.

questions.stem: What is the name of the body part we use to walk?
questions.explanation: We use our legs to walk.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse legs with arms.

questions.stem: Point to the part of your body used for smelling. What is it called?
hints: It is in the middle of your face.
questions.explanation: The nose is used for smelling.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the mouth is for smelling.

questions.stem: Where are your fingers found?
hints: You use them to hold a pencil.
They are at the end of your arms.
questions.explanation: Fingers are found on the hand.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fingers are on the feet.

questions.stem: Which of these is a body part?
hints: Which one is part of you?
questions.explanation: The shoulder is a body part.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think external objects are body parts.

questions.stem: Kofi is touching the part of his body where his arm joins his neck. What part is he touching?
questions.explanation: Kofi is touching his shoulder.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the shoulder with the chest.

questions.stem: Where is your chest located?
options: At the back of your body
On the front of your body between your neck and stomach
hints: It is the front part of your upper body.
questions.explanation: The chest is on the front of the body between the neck and the stomach.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the chest is the same as the stomach.

questions.stem: Which part of the body is used to eat?
questions.explanation: We use the mouth to eat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the nose is used to eat because it is near the mouth.

questions.stem: What do we call the parts at the end of our arms?
questions.explanation: The parts at the end of our arms are the hands.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse hands with feet.

questions.stem: Where are your knees?
hints: You bend them when you walk.
They are in the middle of your legs.
questions.explanation: The knees are found on the legs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse knees with elbows.

questions.stem: Name the body part you use to kick a ball.
hints: It is at the bottom of your body.
questions.explanation: We use our legs (and feet) to kick a ball.

questions.stem: Draw a human head. Label the eyes, nose, and mouth.
hints: Add the features you see on your own face.
questions.explanation: This tests drawing and identifying parts of the face.

questions.stem: Name three parts of the body that are on your face.
questions.explanation: The eyes, nose, mouth, and ears are found on the face.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name body parts not on the face, like knees.

questions.stem: Ama has a pain in the part of her body that connects her head to her shoulders. What part is this?
hints: It is between the head and shoulders.
questions.explanation: The neck connects the head to the shoulders.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the neck with the chest.

questions.stem: Which body parts work together when you clap your hands?
hints: They are at the end of your arms.
questions.explanation: You use your hands to clap.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think you clap with your legs.

questions.stem: Draw a hand and label the fingers.
hints: Draw an outline of your hand.
questions.explanation: This tests drawing and labeling the hand.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an external body part you can see on the outside?
hints: Can you see it from the outside?
questions.explanation: The heart is an internal organ. You cannot see it from the outside.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think they can see their heart because they can feel it beating.

questions.stem: Write down three body parts you use when you wash your face.
hints: What do you use to scrub?
questions.explanation: You use your hands and fingers to wash your face, which includes your eyes and mouth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may list unrelated parts like knees.

questions.stem: Kwame is standing straight. Which body part is touching the ground?
questions.explanation: When standing, the feet touch the ground.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say knees, forgetting that feet are at the very bottom.
